label: WP29 Guidelines on Automated Decision-Making (WP251 rev.01)
citation: Article 29 Working Party WP251 rev.01 (6 February 2018), endorsed by EDPB
body: • "Solely automated" = no meaningful human intervention. Rubber-stamp human review does NOT escape Art. 22.
• The human must have actual authority and competence to change the decision, with access to all relevant information including additional data the subject submits.
• "Legal effects": affects legal rights, status, or eligibility — denial of benefits, contract termination, exclusion from a service.

• "Similarly significantly affects": online credit decisions, e-recruiting without human intervention, dynamic pricing that effectively excludes the subject from a service, behavioural-advertising that exploits vulnerabilities.
• Personalised content recommendations of low-impact products typically don't reach the threshold; but profile-driven exclusion from offers or services may.
• Required safeguards under Art. 22(3): genuine human-intervention route, ability to express the subject's point of view (e.g. submit additional context), ability to contest with appeal mechanism.
• "Meaningful information about the logic" (Art. 13(2)(f), 14(2)(g), 15(1)(h)) ≠ the full algorithm. Must explain: the kind of data used, why the data is relevant, what the consequences are.
